name: Continuous Partial Derivatives Imply Continuity
problem:
For a multivariable function, the existence of the gradient implies continuity.

A sufficient condition for the gradient ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/3a172b4fd0180b172579ebac50f73d8dfb75a219a02b610f666d1a4e446592a2.svg) to exist is that the partial derivatives ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/f20807159d7e3d172a1ed9d92b8001a4c186e78ef3b8423592c75e44b633ec88.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/f423cce200533b35d0f6df2d4a6f5e917529276e749a7ab4995930d64559c98d.svg) both exist in a neighborhood of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/527e0abeb684dd24d8c92e45425542080c4c9493b9460bb89753fef3226c1f92.svg) and are continuous at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/527e0abeb684dd24d8c92e45425542080c4c9493b9460bb89753fef3226c1f92.svg).

Therefore, if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/f20807159d7e3d172a1ed9d92b8001a4c186e78ef3b8423592c75e44b633ec88.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/f423cce200533b35d0f6df2d4a6f5e917529276e749a7ab4995930d64559c98d.svg) both exist in a neighborhood of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/527e0abeb684dd24d8c92e45425542080c4c9493b9460bb89753fef3226c1f92.svg) and are continuous at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/527e0abeb684dd24d8c92e45425542080c4c9493b9460bb89753fef3226c1f92.svg), then ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/bc562d54615dad55d095db2afed7626f62ff7ebf0ab6c5d45471b77ac30b6398.svg) is continuous at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14142143/assets/853e57b0bf9a8f7c16e59d37575ae23ac4028ed66b30720af9d7d49ab595c91b.svg)

**Watch out!** The continuity of the partial derivatives is crucial. The existence of the partial derivatives alone does not imply that a function is continuous at a point.
